extracted.intended_audience: prospective students, current students, faculty, staff, and external stakeholders interested in the Merrill College of Journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional 'About' page describing the Philip Merrill College of Journalism's mission, accreditation, assessment practices, diversity & inclusion policy, program features, and expectations for student learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: College mission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Philip Merrill College of Journalism's mission is to educate students at the undergraduate, master’s and doctoral levels within a liberal arts framework, preparing them for careers in journalism as well as academic research and teaching; to elevate professional and ethical standards of practice; and to advocate for increased knowledge and involvement in democratic processes through dissemination of news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At its core the mission is to improve the production, delivery and access to news and to enhance understanding of journalism's political, cultural and social roles. The College accomplishes this through curriculum, scholarship, and professional service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hallmark — Accurate reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate reporting is listed as a hallmark of good journalism the College stresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the core skills and values the College aims to instill in students as measures of journalistic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hallmark — Good writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Good writing is identified as a core hallmark of journalism education at the College.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasized across coursework and assessment as a key outcome for graduates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hallmark — Technical and analytical skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should gain technical and analytical skills as a central part of their journalism education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 21st-century video and digital storytelling skills, data analysis, and command of relevant technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hallmark — Understanding of media history
rubrics_metrics.description: An understanding of media history is one of the hallmarks the College stresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as necessary context for informed journalistic practice and scholarly work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hallmark — Diversity, law and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: An understanding of diversity, law and ethics is explicitly listed among the hallmarks of good journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as foundational knowledge that should inform reporting, editorial decisions, and professional conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation requirement — ACEJMC and Middle States
rubrics_metrics.description: Merrill College is fully accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications; the College is also subject to Middle States Commission on Higher Education requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These accrediting bodies require programs to directly assess student learning at the course, degree and departmental level; accreditation drives the College's assessment practices and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment levels — course, degree, departmental
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs are required to directly assess student learning at the course, degree and departmental levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment must be implemented across multiple levels of the curriculum rather than relying solely on indirect measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-point rating system for student mastery
rubrics_metrics.description: The College uses a simple five-point rating system to measure students' mastery of the skills, concepts, theories and processes taught in classrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings are applied to student performance on assignments in key courses; aggregated ratings are used to gauge how well students absorb material and to enable comparisons across course sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect measures of student learning
rubrics_metrics.description: The College continues to use indirect measures such as job placement, employer feedback, graduation rates and students’ success in national and regional journalism competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect measures supplement direct assessment data but do not replace the required direct assessments of learning outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation and comparison of assignment ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: By rating student performance on assignments in key courses and aggregating that information, the College gauges mastery and allows for comparisons between sections of a course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation is explicitly used to overcome limitations of grades for cross-section comparisons and to measure course-level learning outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of assessment data to drive curriculum changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment data have resulted in changes in curriculum, including improving consistency of beginning reporting across sections, creating processes to identify and assist students with poor math skills, and providing professional feedback on portfolios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment is iterative: data collection should inform curricular revisions, teaching consistency, and student support interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity is defined as the presence of 'difference,' including race, ethnicity, age, gender, religion, disability, sexual orientation, national origin, and other factors that contribute to individual uniqueness among students, administrators, faculty, and staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition explicitly states that all attributes of diversity derived from knowledge, experiences, ideas and individuals are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusivity means recognizing and respecting differences and understanding that beneath physical differences all are human with the same desires in pursuit of intellectual advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusivity is framed as honoring differences while fostering equal opportunity for intellectual growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting diversity through imagery and spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The College commits to ensuring that its building, websites, staff and promotional images reflect the rich diversity of the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical and online spaces should visibly demonstrate the College's commitment to diversity, inclusion and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching and learning practices to promote diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively promote diversity and inclusion in course syllabi, access to guest speakers, panels, workshops, facilities, resources and services; invite guest speakers and create programs that support diversity and open discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical steps include syllabus content, programming, and access to resources that represent diverse perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring and promotion practices with equity criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively recruit diverse students, staff and faculty by reaching out to organizations (e.g., NABJ, NAHJ, AAJA, NAJA, NLGJA) and aspire to develop evaluation criteria that ensure access and equity are considered in promotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The College intends to codify equity considerations into evaluation and promotion processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student recruitment and advancement strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively seek and encourage a diverse student population by engaging community colleges, diverse high schools, non-traditional university recruitment avenues, and diverse journalism organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment strategies should intentionally extend to non-traditional pipelines and partner organizations to broaden applicant diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty/staff recruitment and retention practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Work to recruit and retain a diverse faculty and staff by promoting an inclusive climate, appointing an Equity Officer for searches, ensuring inclusivity in job descriptions, and striving for diverse search committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity Officer responsibilities include supervising advertisement of positions, ensuring goals of inclusivity are included, and overseeing compliance with university equity policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on implicit bias and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training and mentoring focused on implicit bias, microaggressions, discrimination, and inclusion; include unconscious bias workshops for all faculty, staff and students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should educate on identifying and alleviating explicit and implicit bias across many attributes (age, gender identity, ability, sexual orientation, religion, weight, voice, politics, dress, economics, skin color, race construct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment plan documentation and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: The College has a formal assessment plan (approved spring 2006; updated 2009 and periodically since) and references a full assessment plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment documentation should be maintained, updated to reflect curricular revisions, and accessible for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on fundamentals combined with digital storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: A focus on fundamentals combined with 21st-century video and digital storytelling skills and an innovative, entrepreneurial spirit that journalists need to succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum design should balance traditional fundamentals with contemporary digital competencies and entrepreneurial approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to real-world internships
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to real-world internships in a strong regional media market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internships are positioned as essential experiential learning that connect students with professional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on teaching newsrooms (Capital News Service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunity to work in hands-on, teaching newsrooms in Annapolis, Washington and Baltimore called Capital News Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hands-on newsroom experience is a program feature meant to simulate professional news production for student learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities through specialty centers (investigative and sports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities to do important work with the Howard Center for Investigative Journalism and the Shirley Povich Center for Sports Journalism, nationally recognized centers with real-world publication impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centers provide platforms for students to engage in high-impact reporting projects and specialized training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small class sizes for one-on-one interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Small class sizes that ensure one-on-one interaction with some of the best in journalism education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class size is cited as a structural quality metric that supports individualized instruction and mentorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty composition and professional accomplishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Full-time and part-time faculty include a prestigious mix of journalists and scholars who have won Pulitzers, Emmys and other awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty credentials and professional awards are presented as indicators of instructional quality and industry connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-readiness and diverse career pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: The education prepares students for success in numerous careers; alumni have pursued journalism, law school, entrepreneurship, corporate and nonprofit communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should prepare students with transferable skills valued across multiple professional fields; portfolio feedback and professional feedback are used to enhance career readiness.
